title: SPA/224/2024 of STATE OF UTTARAKHAND AND OTHERS Vs VIJETA JOSHI

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Hon'ble Chief Justice Ms. Ritu Bahri
 Hon'ble Justice Sri Rakesh Thapliyal
 23rd July 2024
Special Appeal No. 224 of 2024
State of Uttarakhand & others ............... Appellant
Vs.
Vijeta Joshi ............Respondent
Counsel for the Appellant: Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned Chief
Standing Counsel

Upon hearing the learned Counsel, the Court made the
following Judgment:
(Per Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
1. The present special appeal has been preferred by the
State against the interim order passed by the learned
Single Judge in WPSS No. 347 of 2024.
2. We perused the interim order passed by the learned
Single Judge dated 12.03.2024, and the learned Single
Judge before passing the interim order sought instruction
from the State and on the basis of the instruction, learned
Single Judge observed in the order particularly in para 9
and 10 that other Data Entry Operators were retained in
service because they approached to this Court by filing
writ petition bearing Writ Petition (S/S) No. 63 of 2023,
Hem Chandra & others vs. State of Uttarakhand & others.
3. In para 10, the learned Single Judge further
observed that respondent/ petitioner was only segregated
for the reason that she has not approached the Court
earlier and consequently, directed respondent nos. 3 and
4 to retain the petitioner/respondent as Date Entry
Operator.

2
4. The learned Single Judge also directed the
respondent/appellant to file their counter affidavit within
six weeks and the matter was ordered to be listed on
03.06.2024.
5. Thereafter, the respondents in compliance to the
order impugned dated 12.03.2024, filed their counter
affidavit and in response thereto rejoinder affidavit has
also been filed.
6. Admittedly, the pleadings are exchanged and the
matter is still pending for consideration before the Writ
Court. Under Chapter VIII Rule 5 of High Court Rules, the
special appeal against the interim order is not
maintainable.
7. Since, pleadings are exchanged in the writ petition
and the matter is still pending before the learned Single
Judge, and further more under Chapter VIII Rule 5 of
High Court Rules the appeal is not maintainable against
the interim order, therefore, we do not find any merit in
the instant appeal, since same is not maintainable.
8. Accordingly, the special appeal is dismissed,
however, we request the learned Single Judge to expedite
the writ petition.
(Ritu Bahri, C.J.)
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) Parul
